title: Single Marine Program
intro: The Single Marine Program (SMP) serves as the voice for single, unaccompanied Marines and any other single active duty servicemember in identifying QOL concerns, developing QOL initiatives, and providing recommendations through advocacy, recreational activities, special events, and community involvement.

sections.markdown:
The program encourages single/unaccompanied Marines to provide input and ideas toward programming for SMP component areas:

• Quality of life (QOL)
• Recreation
• Community involvement

_SMP is sponsored by USAA. MCCS Sponsors. No Federal or DoD endorsement implied._

sections.markdown: Convenient on-demand training videos that instruct Unit Representatives and SMP Executive Council Members about the Single Marine Program.

sections.heading: Training Videos
sections.markdown:
The purpose of this training is to conveniently instruct Unit Representatives and elected SMP Executive Council Members about the Single Marine Program. The SMP Marine will view this training, and discuss lessons learned with the Marines in their respective unit. This training can be accessed anywhere.

• [Part 1 of 3: SMP Structure](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nv-0BOS_ikA&list=PLZAWLbxP7RPKGq3lPgJl6vb-bdzZMUu2o&index=2)
• [Part 2 of 3: Pillars of SMP](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bReWDIvemE0&list=PLZAWLbxP7RPKGq3lPgJl6vb-bdzZMUu2o&index=1)
• [Part 3 of 3: Role of SMP Council](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sq7fVAg5C_c&list=PLZAWLbxP7RPKGq3lPgJl6vb-bdzZMUu2o&index=3)

To view our PME/Training schedule, view the SMP Calendar.

sections.heading: Reoccurring Volunteerism with Youth Sports
sections.markdown:
**Youth Sports Coaches Needed**

Helping to build young athletes is about so much more than sports. As a leader and role model, you have an opportunity to impact young lives as they improve their skills both on and off the court or field. If you're looking to make a difference, contact our Youth Sports office for more information.

Please call 910-451-2177 or email MCCSLejeuneYouthSports@usmc-mccs.org.

sections.heading: Where do I find volunteer opportunities?
sections.markdown: Visit the [USMC Volunteer Coordinator page](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building-training) or the [Single Marine Program Volunteer Opportunities page](https://lejeunenewriver.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/single-marine-program/smp-volunteer-opportunities) to see the volunteer opportunities calendar.

sections.heading: How do I request volunteers for an event on or off base?
sections.markdown: Visit the USMC Volunteer Coordinator page or the Single Marine Program page and submit an online request for volunteers. You will indicate in your request whether the event is on base or at an offsite location.

sections.heading: Who do I contact to receive my Letter of Appreciation (LOA)?
sections.markdown: Please contact the agency that you volunteered for to receive your LOA. If the event was coordinated by the Single Marine Program, please email LejeuneSMPVolunteerProgram@usmc-mccs.org about your Letter of Appreciation.

sections.heading: How do I earn the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal (MOVSM)?
sections.markdown: Visit the USMC Volunteer Coordinator page for more information.

sections.heading: How do I track my hours for the President's Volunteer Service Award?
sections.markdown: Please keep a personal record of your volunteer hours for each month. Please track each organization you volunteer with and the number of hours you provide. At the end of the calendar year, you will have an opportunity to submit your hours for the President's Volunteer Service Award here on our Volunteer Coordinator web page.

sections.heading: Who is eligible to volunteer?
sections.markdown: Any service member with the permission of your command, civilian/DOD employees and their family members.
